title: rbac-v2: enforce KMS region residency + audit logging hardening
author: Samantha Lee
release_notes: Enforce KMS region residency policy at RBAC v2 evaluation time and improve audit logging granularity for KMS-related actions. No behavioral change for customers already compliant; admins may need to update policies for multi-region keys.
description: Context / Motivation: We have multiple customer reports and internal audits showing gaps in region-residency enforcement for RBAC v2 KMS bindings. This PR closes the gap by validating KMS key region constraints during RBAC v2 policy evaluation and by hardening audit events emitted for key-usage and policy-evaluation paths. Changes include runtime policy checks, denial-by-default behavior for cross-region key use, and richer audit records for forensic tracing. Checklist: - [x] Add region-residency check to rbac evaluator - [x] Emit detailed audit events for kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:Sign, kms:Verify with policy_id, key_id, region, evaluated_decision - [x] Add feature-flag to opt-out for back-compat during rollout (rbac.v2.enforce_kms_residency) - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering multi-region scenarios - [x] Update docs and operator migration notes - [x] Run infra canary on dedicated and private clusters Implementation notes: - RBAC evaluator: added a KMSResidencyRule that consults the policy bindings and key metadata (from key registry service cache). If a key's region does not match the allowed residency specified on the resource binding, the evaluator returns Deny with a new reason code KMS_REGION_MISMATCH. - Audit logging: audit service schema extended (non-breaking) to include fields: event_subject (policy_id), resource_region, key_region, residency_requirement, decision_reason. Logs are emitted at INFO for allowed actions and WARN for denied/denial-by-policy. - Feature flagging: rbac.v2.enforce_kms_residency defaults to false in the rollout; ops can opt-in per-cluster using the config service. - Migration: operators with multi-region KMS setups must either pin keys to allowed regions or enable the feature and update RBAC bindings to list allowed key regions. Testing: added unit tests for evaluator rules, mocks for key registry responses, and integration tests that run the policy flow end-to-end. Related: Linear ENG-4981, SEC-227.
